title: Golden Honeycomb Toffee
summary: Light, crunchy honeycomb toffee made by whisking bicarbonate of soda into light golden caramel and letting it set into a bubble-filled slab.

steps.title: Prepare first
steps.text: Oil the tray and line it with baking paper. Sift the bicarbonate into the small bowl to remove lumps and keep the whisk beside the stove; the final steps take seconds.

steps.title: Dissolve the sugar
steps.text: Put the sugar, corn syrup and water in the deep pan over medium heat and stir until the sugar has dissolved.

steps.title: Boil to 149 °C
steps.text: Stop stirring, turn the heat to medium-high and boil for 10-12 min, until the syrup is light gold and reads 149 °C.

steps.title: Whisk in the bicarbonate
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, add the bicarbonate and whisk for no more than 5 seconds. The caramel foams up dramatically, so use a deep pan.

steps.title: Pour without spreading
steps.text: Pour it straight onto the tray and leave it where it lands. Spreading or pressing knocks out the bubbles.

steps.title: Leave to set
steps.text: Leave it undisturbed for about 1 h, until cold and crisp right through, then break it into chunks.

tips: The most common mistake is over-whisking after the bicarbonate goes in; the foam collapses and the honeycomb turns dense, so stop after 5 seconds.
Use fresh bicarbonate of soda; an old packet gives a flat, heavy result.
Humidity makes honeycomb sticky, so break and store it as soon as it is cold.
Dip pieces in melted dark chocolate for a homemade chocolate honeycomb bar.
storage: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 1 week; it softens quickly if left out.
